title: Dock Anything, Take a Photo, Smoother Bars
summary: Put any tool or command on the touch puck and the radial menu's dots, take a photo for On a Photo, and work with contextual bars that fit the screen.
new: Dock Any Tool or Command
In Preferences, edit the Touch Puck or the radial menu's dots, tap a place and type: any tool or Loupe command can sit there.
Touch Puck Editor
Preferences > Touch Puck > Edit shows the puck's places large: drag a button onto a place or between places, or tap to choose.
Take a Photo
On a Photo can use the camera as well as a photo you choose.
Isometric Patterns
Isometric, Iso Cubes, Iso Stars and Iso Weave in the Pattern Gallery.
Display Settings
Choose ProMotion 120 Hz or 60 Hz, and Battery Saver for longer sessions.
improved: Contextual Bars
Taller with wider sliders, they float over the page and fit any screen, widening a slider while you drag it.
Curve Pen
Smoother curves with no jagged facets, and Edit Curve works on a line on any layer.
Docked Panels
An unpinned panel folds to its bar when you touch the page, instead of closing.
Radial Menu Arcs
Arc labels rest as a small icon and show their name while you drag.
fixed: The Radial Menu and Touch Puck previews no longer cover the settings on an upright iPad.

title: Settings Where You Work
summary: A big polish build from a live testing night. Each tool's settings now sit in one bar under the top bar, Preferences is roomier and folds into sections, and the touch puck and radial menu are easier to set up.
new: Tool Settings Bar
The tool in hand shows its settings in one bar under the top bar: Size and Stabiliser for brushes, modes, Gap and Lines for the Paint Bucket, This Layer or All Layers for the Lasso.
Touch Puck in Preferences
Its own page with a live preview: choose which buttons sit around the puck, and set its size, halo and buttons, which now work together.
More Places to Dock
Panels can dock in the middle of a side at card size, or centred along the bottom, as well as full height.
Try It Switches
Under Try It, tiles turn each stroke setting on or off, and a Symmetry button mirrors your test lines or not.
improved: Preferences
Bigger, one size on every page, settings grouped into sections that fold and remember, Background now part of Appearance, and a clearer build number.
Radial Menu
The preview shows the real size, the size reads in the middle ring, and slider labels no longer sit on other buttons.
Layer Menu
Long press a layer for a menu with icons that always stays on screen. Dragging a layer shows where it will land.
Loupe
Every result says whether it is a Tool, a Panel or a Preference. The Mini Loupe opens without the keyboard.
fixed: Filling the page undoes in one step, and asks first when there is drawing on the page.
A new layer's picture no longer flashes black.

title: Join on the Toolbar
summary: A small test build. Join gets its own button under Trim and works anywhere in a pattern. Join is for testing here; the App Store edition still leaves it out for now.
new: Join on the Left Toolbar
Join sits just under Trim. Circle two line ends that nearly meet and they join in one clean point. You can also put it on a radial menu dot, or find it in Loupe.
improved: Segments Slider
2 to 12 segments now fill the first third of the slider, so small counts are easy to pick.
fixed: Circling ends on any copy of a symmetry or wallpaper joins them. Ends on another visible layer are found too, ends that already meet get a short message, and a short line inside the circle is no longer folded onto itself.
A fine wallpaper on a wide (4K) canvas now reaches the edges.

title: Tester Build of Release Candidate 2
summary: The same app as build 147, built for testing. Testers get the App Store version's tools, with Bismuth Full open; tap the build number in Preferences, About five times for the Developer options.
improved: The App Store Tool Set
Tools held back from the first App Store release no longer show for testers, and neither does the Experimental section.
Developer Options
Preferences, About: tap the build number five times. Developer, Edition has As Built, Free, Full and All Tools (every tool, held-back ones too).

title: Release Candidate 2
summary: Build 146 with three fixes for the App Store edition, so it passes Apple's upload check.
improved: Support Instead of Feedback
In the App Store edition, Preferences, About offers Privacy Policy and Support; Send Feedback stays in test builds.
fixed: The build includes the permission texts Apple's upload check requires, worded for every edition.
The older Add Text sheet no longer shows in the App Store edition, which holds text back for now.

title: Release Candidate: Trim Everywhere, Lattice Preview and Clearer Panels
summary: The first candidate for the App Store: Trim works on every copy of a pattern, Lattice can be previewed for 5 minutes, the puck can be resized, and labels stay readable on glass. This build behaves exactly as the App Store edition.
new: Preview Lattice
Lattice joins the tools you can try for 5 minutes before unlocking. It opens straight away when the Preview starts.
Puck Size
Preferences, Pencil & Touch: Puck Size, Halo Distance and Button Size, and Reset Puck Size. Loupe has Touch Puck Size.
Add Colour Stops
The + beside Reverse adds a colour stop to any gradient.
improved: Wallpaper Under Symmetry
In the Pattern panel, Wallpaper now sits right under Symmetry.
Gradient Fill Panel
Shape and Fill fold open like the Pattern panel's sections, with a summary of what is set, and the hints are easier to read.
Readable on Glass
With Liquid Glass panels, the smaller labels are brighter, so they read well over a light page.
Free Edition Tag
Welcome, About and What's New show a small tag: Free Edition, or Full after the unlock.
Lattice and Eyedropper
Both are now on for everyone.
fixed: Trim now cuts lines made by Symmetry, Repeat and Wallpaper anywhere on the page. Before, it stopped working away from the first few copies.

title: Founder Edition, New Icons and One Pattern Switch
summary: New icons to choose from, a Founder Edition icon for everyone who helped shape Bismuth before launch, one switch for every pattern, and construction lines that come out fine.
new: Founder Edition Icon
Thank you for testing Bismuth. Preferences, Appearance, App Icon has a Founder Edition icon that stays yours when Bismuth reaches the App Store.
Choose Your App Icon
Preview, Free and, with Bismuth Full, the Full icon in black glass. Loupe has Change App Icon too.
One Pattern Switch
The eye at the end of the Pattern button hides every pattern, and shows it again exactly as it was, grid and all. The Pattern panel has the same switch beside its title.
improved: Fine Construction Lines
Placing a construction as lines draws fine lines like the guides, whatever the brush size.
Panels and the Rail Get Along
With a panel docked beside the tools, the tool rail's panels open on top of it, and the touch puck steps out from under it.
Lattice Button
Lattice in the top bar is now a button as large as Pattern.
Lift Has Its Own Icon
Lift Last Stroke to a New Layer shows a stroke lifting off a layer, in lilac, so it no longer looks like Layers.
Free Edition or Full
Welcome, About and What's New say which edition you have.
Fold the Puck
The eye at the bottom of the touch puck folds its buttons away, and brings them back.
Add Colour Stops
The + beside Reverse adds a colour stop to any gradient, in the middle of the widest gap. Tapping the strip still adds one where you tap.
fixed: With a large brush, Flower of Life and the other constructions no longer turn into a solid shape when placed as lines.

title: Ready for the App Store: Free Edition and Preview
summary: The free edition and Bismuth Full are set for the first App Store release, and free users can try a Full drawing tool for 5 minutes before unlocking it.
new: Preview a Full Tool

In the free edition, picking a Bismuth Full tool shows a short offer. Tap Preview for 5 Minutes to draw with it for real; a bar at the top shows the time left and an Unlock button. Each tool can be previewed once a day, and what you draw stays.
Bismuth Full Lesson
Learn, Start Here: what the free edition holds, how Preview works and how to restore the purchase.
improved: What Is Free and What Is Full

Symmetry with no limits, the Pattern Gallery, the everyday brushes, Fill and up to three layers are free. Constructions, My Patterns, Gradient Fill and Fill Through Outlines, Offset, Dashes, Simplify and Convert are now part of Bismuth Full. Test builds still open everything.
Menus With Icons
Holding a drawing, stack, lattice, layer or motif opens a menu with an icon beside every choice.

title: Panels Your Way, Smarter Fill and Loupe
summary: Move, fold and dock panels where your hand is not, save your own patterns and gradients, fill tiny gaps with ease, erase through filled shapes, and find any command with Loupe.
new: Loupe (Experimental)

Switch on Loupe in Preferences, Experimental, and tap the magnifying glass on the right toolbar. Every command in one list, with what fits your tool and layer first. Write in the search box with Apple Pencil, or press Command-K with a keyboard and use the arrow keys.
Dock Panels Anywhere

Drag a panel by the tab on its top edge to move it, and drop it on an edge or a corner to dock it there. Tap the tab to fold a panel to a small bar that still shows its value. Drawing Hand in Preferences keeps panels away from your hand.
My Patterns
The bookmark in the Pattern panel saves your pattern. Hold its card to rename it. See All has My Patterns, Recent and Ready tabs.
Save Gradients
The bookmark in any gradient editor saves the gradient; saved ones come first among the cards.
Fill Tiny Gaps
With Fill, tap close to a small gap to fill it, drag across many gaps to fill them all, or circle an area to fill every gap inside.
Fill Through Outlines
The LINES chip on Fill and Gradient Fill takes the outline into the fill, so one solid shape is left.
Simplify and Convert Layers
In a layer's menu: Simplify joins fills with their outlines, Convert to Shapes and Convert to Lines change what the layer holds.
Layer Groups for Lattices
A lattice sent to your drawing arrives as one group: hide it, fold it, rename it or move all of it at once.
improved: Eraser Cuts Through Fills
Erasing part of a filled shape now cuts a clean channel through it instead of removing the whole shape.
Snap, Then Steer

After holding to snap, keep the Pencil down: a line's end catches every 15 degrees, an arc slides along its circle, and shapes turn and grow until you lift. Snap Joins Line Ends has its own switch next to Clean Joins.
Pattern Panel

All Off switches every pattern off and remembers how they were. Wallpaper and Grid are separate sections, and switching a section on opens it. The arc of pattern buttons is back on Edit on Page. A warning shows when the layer already has drawing.
Gradient Editor
Picture cards first, See All, and Shape in a section that folds, like the Pattern panel. Stops catch at quarter points. Remove, Reverse and Save are small icons.
Slider Stops
Sliders across the app catch at sensible points: 25, 50 and 75 percent, 100 percent, and 0 and 90 degrees.
Trim
Trim has its own button under the line tools.
Text (Experimental)
The radial menu has the Text tool's settings, colour changes selected text, drag to move the caret or select, and text on a path can sit above or below the line.
Lattice
A cleaner panel with sections that fold, colour dots at the top, a Recursion section, and Surprise Me keeps shapes light. Surprise Colours picks colours on its own.
Gallery
Pinch to see more drawings at once, or bigger ones. Lattice pictures load faster.
Fewer Words
Gradient Fill's notes are short lines with icons, and Lock Aspect is a lock icon.
fixed: Drawings save more safely and fall back to their backup if a file is damaged.

title: Gradients, Eyedropper and Lattice
summary: Paint with gradients, pick exact colours with a new Eyedropper, keep a lattice in your drawing with one tap, and tune paper textures.
new: Gradient Fill
A new Gradient Fill tool sits with Fill. Drag across the page or a shape to fill it with a gradient, previewed as you drag.
Gradient Line Colour
Hold a layer in Layers and pick Line Colour: Gradient to colour every line on it with one gradient across the page.
Eyedropper
Its own tool with a magnifier: it picks the colour you see, and you can hold and drag to choose.
Paper Texture Sliders
Change a paper texture's Size, Grit and Strength, or tap New Grain for a fresh pattern.
Setting Cards
Each stroke setting has its own card with a live sample, and Try It in Preferences, Drawing.
improved: One Gradient Editor
The Gradient brush, Gradient Fill, line colour and Lattice's Colour by Level share one gradient editor.
Lattice Done Keeps Your Lattice
Done adds the lattice to your drawing as new layers. Export, Save to Lattices and New Drawing are in the Lattice top bar, and Lattice opens from a diamond button beside Pattern.
One Pattern Button
The top bar has one Pattern button, with a Pattern panel beside the page.
Motifs in Your Colour
Stamped motifs take the pen colour; switch COLOUR to Own to keep their own colours.
fixed: Done now hides the keyboard in Developer Review.

title: Grid Builder, Layered Export and Text
summary: Build patterns in one place with the Grid Builder, export with your layers to Photoshop, Illustrator and Affinity, type right on the page, fill the page, and undo even after reopening a drawing.
new: Grid Builder

The Grid Builder button in the top bar puts every pattern control on one screen: Rotate, Mirror, Repeat, Grid, Fade, Constructions and Presets along the bottom. Drag the centre ring to move the guides, and double-tap it to put them back in the middle.
Export With Layers
SVG, PDF and a new Photoshop PSD export keep your layers and their names, with the paper on a layer of its own. They open in Affinity, Illustrator and Photoshop.
Text on the Page (Experimental)
Switch on Text Tool in Preferences, Experimental. Tap where the text should start and type, tap text to change it, type along a line or circle, and turn text into shapes with Create Outlines.
Page Backgrounds
Give the page a colour, a gradient, a paper texture or a picture from the Page row in Layers. Fill now fills an empty layer, or the page itself.
Undo After Reopening
Each drawing keeps its last 50 steps, so Undo still works when you open it again. Change the number in Preferences, Drawing.
Stripes and Wallpaper Patterns
Grid has a new Stripes layout, and Make It Fit lines your symmetry up with the tiles so lines meet across them. New presets: Square Mirror, Triangles and Stripes Mirror.
improved: One Grid Button
Tile and Grid are now one Grid button, with Repeat My Drawing and Guide Only in its panel.
Tile Width, Height and Angle
Set a tile's width and height with Lock Aspect, and turn the grid with Snap 15° and quick angles.
Constructions in the Top Bar
Constructions moved to the top bar. Show one as a guide behind your drawing, or place it as lines.
Guides in Every Tile
With a grid on, every tile shows its own symmetry lines and repeat circles.
The Same Gestures Everywhere
Two-finger undo, three-finger redo, pinch, turn and double-tap to fit now work the same in Lattice, 3D Body Preview, Print Stencil and the feedback screenshot.
A Tidier Top Bar
A line splits each button from its options arrow, and on smaller iPads the bar stays on one row.
fixed: The Repeat circles now stay fixed to the page while you zoom, and Twist shows as the circles turn.
Turning a grid no longer leaves bare corners on the page.

title: Lattice and Pencil Touches
summary: Lattice thumbnails show their real colours, New on the Lattices tab starts a lattice, and a double-tap on your Pencil does what you chose in Settings.
improved: Pencil Double-Tap Follows Your Settings

On Apple Pencil Pro and Apple Pencil (2nd generation), a double-tap now does what you picked in the iPad's Settings, Apple Pencil: switch to the eraser, back to your last tool, open the colour panel, or nothing.
Pictures on the Lasso Bar
Edit Curve, Mirror, Dashes and Offset each have a small picture beside the word, so they are quicker to tell apart.
Lattice Buttons
From a drawing, Send to Canvas and Send to a New Drawing sit side by side at the same size.
fixed: On the Lattices tab of the gallery, New now opens a new lattice instead of a new drawing.
Gallery thumbnails show every formation in its own colour, with Colour by Level, including after Save as a New Lattice or Overwrite.

title: Ready for iPadOS 27
summary: Built with Apple's newest tools for iPadOS 27, with steadier saving underneath. Everything from build 136 is included.
improved: Built for iPadOS 27
Bismuth is now built with Apple's iPadOS 27 tools, which the App Store will require from April 2027.

title: Your Review Fixes
summary: Fixes from the build 135 iPad review: calmer notices, steadier snapped lines, safer Lattice saving and easier tools to find.
new: Surprise Colours
A palette button beside the dice in Lattice gives the chosen formation fresh colours that go together.
Overwrite or Save as New
Tap Done after changing a saved lattice and choose whether to update it or keep a new copy.
Recolour Marks in Notes
In Add Note, tap any mark you made and pick a colour to change it. Saved notes reopen with their marks still editable.
improved: Notices Stay Out of the Way
Messages float on their own layer, larger, and no longer push the toolbars down. A small mark knocks beside your Pencil so you see it even when your hand covers the top.
Tool Families Open Beside the Toolbar
The other tools in a family slide out as a second column next to the toolbar instead of over it.
Offset Is Easier to Find
Offset shows whenever a line or outline is selected, and works on every selected line at once.
Lasso Bar
Deselect is a word at the start of the bar, away from Delete, and Recolour is a colour circle.
Lattice
A Canvas button at the top left takes you back, Done stands out, Surprise Me makes calmer shapes, and lines can be twice as thick.
Zoom Out on Notes
The feedback screenshot can zoom out past full size.
fixed: A line straightened by holding no longer shifts a little as you lift the Pencil.
A lattice with no colour chosen no longer draws white lines when the pen is white.
Done no longer saves a new lattice when you were editing a saved one.
Lattice Could Vanish on a Pinch
Pinching after a double-tap no longer jumps to a view with nothing in it, and a lattice pushed off the screen slides back.

title: Lattice Formations
summary: Stack several shapes in one lattice, each with its own colour, and find colour in one tap.
new: Lattice Formations
Layer up to six shapes in one lattice. Each formation has its own form, drawing settings and colours, and lands on its own layers when you send it.
Surprise Me
Tap the dice in Lattice for a random shape to explore from.
improved: Lattice Colour Is Easier to Find
Colour has its own tab, and two swatches in Lattice's top bar open the line and point colours straight away.
Lattice Thumbnails
Saved lattices show every formation.

title: Dashes and Dots
summary: Turn any line into even dashes or dots, and a few more touches for Join Ends and Lattice.
new: Dashes and Dots
Lasso a line and tap Dashes to turn it into evenly spaced dashes or dots. Set the length and gap, and the pattern is fitted to the line.
improved: Lattice Remembers Fade
Fade Deeper Levels is now saved with each lattice.

title: Join Ends, Motif Along a Line and Lattice Colours
summary: Join line ends in one move, repeat a motif along a line, colour your lattices, and export masks as true vectors.
new: Join Ends (Experimental)
With the Trim tool set to Join, circle two line ends that nearly meet and they join in one clean point. Switch it on in Preferences, Experimental.
Motif Along a Line (Experimental)
Draw a line with the Stamp tool and a set number of motifs land evenly along it, or all the way round a closed loop. Switch it on in Preferences, Experimental.
Repeat
After you Duplicate and place a copy, tap Repeat to add more copies by the same step, for an even row, ring or spiral.
Lattice Colours
Pick colours for lines and points, blend them level by level with Colour by Level, and send a lattice straight to a new drawing.
Zoom the Feedback Screenshot
On Add Note, pinch with two fingers to zoom, turn and slide the screenshot. Tap Fit to see it all again.
improved: Hold to Snap Joins Line Ends
When a held curve snaps, an end that stops just short of another line's end is carried on to meet it.
Off-Centre Motifs
A motif drawn away from the centre now stamps at full size, right under the Pencil.
Lattice Thumbnails
Saved lattices show their saved line colour.
fixed: Masks and clipped layers now export as you see them, still as clean vectors.
Round line ends no longer show a small white notch.

title: Markup Tools, Mirror Curve and Even Offsets
summary: Mark up feedback like a pro, mirror a curve with one tap, and add perfectly even parallel lines.
new: Feedback Markup Tools
Add text notes with numbers, arrows, boxes, rings and a highlighter to feedback screenshots, in six colours, with a puck for quick tool changes.
Mirror Curve
After a curve snaps smooth, tap Mirror Curve beside the puck to add its matching side.
Offset
Lasso a line or outline and tap Offset to add an even, parallel copy at a set distance.
Close My Line
Finish a stroke near its start and it joins up smoothly, keeping curves curved.
Drag Colour to Fill
Drag the colour circle onto a shape to fill it.
Ready Stencil Widget
Your last drawing on the Home Screen, one tap from Print Stencil.
Large Quick Start Widget
Adds New Pattern and Print Stencil, and New Lattice when Lattice is switched on.
improved: Faster Gallery
Thumbnails load in the background, so large galleries open and scroll more smoothly.
Faster Print Stencil
The preview no longer freezes the screen on large prints, and the gap check is quicker.
Faster Saved Lattices
Saved lattice previews no longer freeze the gallery.
Tool Families Open Downward
Brush and tool choices open over the toolbar, where your hand does not cover them.
Clearer Transform Guides
Snap guides are dashed and the turn handle has its own colour.
Clearer Size Readout
The size and stabiliser readouts are easier to read.
Clearer Switches
Switches now show a visible track when off.
Clip Icon
Clip has its own hand-drawn icon.
Version in About
Preferences shows the version with the build number.
fixed: A dots fill no longer spills over the open page.
Clean Joins is the same colour on the puck as on the radial menu.
The motif panel now scrolls instead of running off the screen.

title: Private Feedback, Cleaner Cuts and Stencil Marks
summary: Your artwork stays out of feedback, the eraser cuts cleanly, and stencils are easier to line up.
new: Artwork Hidden From Feedback
Feedback screenshots hide your artwork, photos and drawing names unless you choose to include them.
Alignment Marks
Print Stencil can add a centre cross and edge marks to help line up a stencil.
Gap Check
Print Stencil warns when lines sit too close together at the finished size.
Circle to Trim
Circle a leftover dot or piece with Trim to remove it.
Known Issues
What's New now lists the problems we know about, with ways around them.
Widget Tour
A picture guide to each widget and how to add it.
Privacy Policy and Support
Find both in Preferences, under About.
improved: Cleaner Eraser
Erasing part of a line now leaves a clean, flat cut.
App Icon
The icon no longer shows a second edge inside its corners.
fixed: Undo and redo now work properly while placing and editing curves.
A two-finger tap now undoes while Draw with a Finger is on.

title: Widgets
summary: Your drawings and a daily idea, right on your Home Screen.
new: Recent Drawings Widget
Jump back into the drawings you worked on last.
Quick Start Widget
Start a new drawing, continue your last one, or open a lesson. It also fits the Lock Screen.
Daily Pattern Widget
A new symmetry idea each day. Tap to start drawing it.

title: Your iPad Review, Fixed
summary: Controls answer every tap, stencils print what you see, and fills stay inside the lines.
new: Pinch Back to Your View
Double-tap to fit the page, then pinch outward to return to where you were.
Feedback From Anywhere
Start Feedback Mode from the drawing, review saved notes on its bar and edit them later.
Two New Lessons
Learn to steady your lines and fill shapes that have small gaps.
improved: Clearer Tour and Lessons
The screen dims only when pointing at a control, and the tour now has a Back button.
Print Stencil Preview
Pinch, rotate and drag to look closer.
Bigger Airbrush
The airbrush now goes up to 600.
Lattice
Pinch and rotate like the main canvas, and your work saves itself when you close it.
Back Where You Left Off
The app reopens the drawing you were working on.
fixed: Tools no longer look selected or ignore a tap after a touch is interrupted.
Strokes of the same solid colour now print as one clean outline.
Fill closes tiny gaps instead of flooding the page.
Move now moves only what you selected.
With symmetry off, the eraser cuts only the line under it.

title: Learn Bismuth
summary: Short hands-on lessons show you how each feature works.
new: Learn Bismuth
A library of short lessons that run on a practice page.
Show Me
What's New now leads straight to lessons for the latest features.
improved: Clearer Tour
The tour dims the screen around the exact control and names it.

title: Stencils That Match the Page
summary: Print Stencil now follows your clipped layers and masks.
fixed: Print Stencil now prints only what shows on the page, and mask layers no longer print as ink.

title: Your Choice on AI
summary: You now decide each time whether Claude may read the feedback you send.
new: Let Claude Read This Feedback
A switch on the send screen, off by default. Leave it off and your email is marked so Claude does not read it.
improved: A Lighter First Launch
New installs start with a plain background, so the app stays quick on older iPads until you choose one.

title: Feedback As You Test
summary: Testers can capture the screen, mark it up and write or dictate notes without leaving the app.
new: Feedback Mode
Capture the screen, mark it up, cover anything private and add a note. Send all your notes together when you are done.
improved: Private Logs
The app's log no longer records the names of your drawings.

title: A Tour That Sets Up Your Tools
summary: The guided tour now asks which Pencil you use and lets you make the radial menu your own.
new: Your Pencil
The tour checks for squeeze and hover, then sets the app up for Apple Pencil Pro, another Apple Pencil or no Pencil.
Your Radial Menu
Choose what the radial menu shows, how large it is and which tools sit on it, with a live preview.
improved: Opening the Radial Menu
Without a squeeze, tapping the touch puck now opens the radial menu after setup.

title: Fits Every iPad, and a Tour You Can Retake
summary: The drawing screen now fits smaller iPads in portrait, the tour lets you choose your background, and your work is better protected while you draw.
new: Choose Your Background
The guided tour now lets you pick a background or switch it off.
Take the Tour Again
Find the tour in the gallery, the … menu and Preferences > About. It always opens on a fresh page.
Drawing Backups
Each drawing keeps a backup that opens if the drawing can no longer be read.
improved: Autosave
Your work now saves during long stretches of steady drawing, without waiting for a pause.
VoiceOver
Rail buttons, the touch puck and its buttons now have spoken names.
fixed: The top bar now fits on two rows, so the left toolbar stays at the edge and every button can be reached.
A bad point in a stroke can no longer stop a drawing from saving.
The app now tells you when masks and clipping will be left out of the file.

title: Safer Saves and a Speed Report
summary: The app now tells you if a drawing could not be saved, and Send Feedback can include a report of how smoothly the app ran.
new: Speed Report
With Crashes and Slowdowns or Everything Helpful chosen, the app measures how smoothly it runs. The report stays on your iPad and only goes with Send Feedback.
improved: Clearer Labels
Lattice settings and a few other labels now use consistent capitals.
fixed: If a drawing cannot be saved, the app now warns you and tries again.
Open panels now sit on top of the puck, so it no longer covers their controls.

title: A Lighter, Faster Canvas
summary: The canvas now rests when nothing is happening and only redraws what changes, so long sessions stay smooth and the iPad stays cooler.
improved: Long Sessions
The canvas rests when you pause and wakes the moment you touch it, and the app eases off when the iPad gets hot or Low Power Mode is on.
Drawing Over Heavy Art
A stroke in progress no longer redraws everything under it, so busy drawings and airbrush layers stay responsive.
Airbrush
Long airbrush strokes only work out their newest dabs as you go.
Finishing a Stroke
Layer thumbnails and autosave pictures are made in the background, so lifting the Pencil no longer waits for them.
Opening Screens
The animated background is prepared once, so the gallery and other screens open faster.

title: A Tour That Shows You
summary: The tour now points at each control and picks the tool for you to try.
improved: Tour
Each step circles the control it talks about and selects the tool to try, for example Trim; at the end you are back on the pen.

title: Ready for the App Store
summary: Getting ready for release: a welcome and a short tour, experimental tools you choose to switch on, the one-time purchase, Send Feedback, crystal themes and backgrounds, radial menu settings, and a calmer, more consistent look.
new: Welcome and Tour
A welcome screen and a short hands-on tour on first launch; each step ticks itself off as you do it.
Experimental Tools
Lattice, Live Trace, 3D Body Preview and Preview on a Photo are switched on or off in Preferences › Experimental, or on the last page of the tour.
Bismuth Background
Branching bismuth crystals grow, meet and fade. It is the new default; the stepped Hopper crystals are there too.
Background Settings
Size and Speed for every background, plus Branching or Steps and Density for the crystal ones, in Preferences › Background.
Radial Menu Settings
Choose the rings, arcs and tools the radial menu shows, its size and its opening animation, with a live preview.
Bismuth Full
One purchase unlocks everything, with no subscription; see your edition and restore a purchase in Preferences.
Send Feedback
Sends a note with the build and the app's log, with or without a screenshot. Help Grow Bismuth sets what the app keeps to share.
Crystal Themes
Twelve themes named after crystals, with Bismuth as the default and Selenite as a light theme.
Mirror for Transfer
Print Stencil can mirror the design for transfer paper and turn it sideways on the page.
improved: Swirl Background
Redrawn from scratch, keeping its slow, painted look.
One Switch Everywhere
Every on and off switch is the same glass switch, matching the sliders.
Selected Tool
The highlight sits evenly in the rail's rounded corner, follows the Corners setting and turns to glass with Liquid Glass.
Gallery Bar
Developer, What's New and Folder are icon buttons with hover labels.
Lattice
Its own drawn icon, depth up to 10 (or 16 with Unlimited), and a haptic on every slider.
Smoother Airbrush
The finished picture is kept ready, so menus and sliders stay smooth over heavy shading, and dabs fade softly at the edge.
Radial Menu
Flow and Edge show as icons; holding a control grows it into its settings.
Themes
The hex field locks until tapped, with copy and paste buttons and a Done button.
Corners
More room from the screen corners in landscape.
fixed: One tap could skip two cards of the tour; each tap now moves one card.

title: Lighter airbrush, landscape that fits
summary: From the build 115 iPad test: the airbrush no longer slows the app, landscape fits the screen, the tools from the lower left move to the right, and Print Stencil, themes and Lattice are clearer.
new: Corner Points in Edit Curve
Tap the centre of a point to make it a sharp corner; tap again to make it smooth.
Several Custom Themes
Make as many themes as you like, each with its own name, and rename or delete them.
Tracing Image Eye
An eye under the Tracing Image button hides and shows it in one tap; its panel has Hide and Show too.
Lattice Zoom
Pinch to zoom and drag to pan the Lattice preview; double-tap to fit it again.
improved: Faster Airbrush
Each airbrush dab is now one soft shape drawn by the graphics chip instead of six stacked discs, about fifty times fewer points, so layers of shading no longer slow the sliders or the background.
Bigger Airbrush
The airbrush goes up to 240 and keeps its own size, separate from the line tools.
Radial Menu Follows the Airbrush
With the airbrush in hand the dial's lower arcs are Flow and Edge, and the rope and clean-up switches are left out.
Airbrush and Zen Icons
The airbrush has its own drawn icon, and Zen mode is a singing bowl instead of the ensō.
Landscape
The rails pack tighter on a shorter screen, so the top bar and every tool fit in landscape.
Right-Hand Rail
Text, Import, Live Trace, Print Stencil, the previews and Lattice move from the lower left rail to the right, under Tracing Image and Shape Builder.
Print Stencil
Starts at Fit to One Page, says the finished size and page count in plain words, folds every section, and previews sharp at small sizes.
Theme Colours
Themes and the custom accent use the app's own colour picker, and Preferences shows a short row of themes with Show All.
Lattice
A quick preview while you change a setting and the full drawing a moment after; depth stops where the points would run away; switches match the rest of the app.
fixed: Erasing part of, trimming, recolouring, copying or merging an airbrush stroke keeps its soft edge instead of turning it into a hard line.
The curve pen's icon shows in the bar above the page again.

title: Lines that meet, and a quieter page
summary: Small gaps close, curves cross mirror lines smoothly, and Zen mode clears the screen down to the tools, the page and a three-button puck.
new: Close Small Gaps
When a line ends just short of another line's end, or of a line, it is drawn on to meet it, with the correction spread over its last few points. A switch in Preferences › Drawing.
Smooth Across Mirror Lines

When a stroke ends close to a mirror line, its last stretch bends to meet the line square on, so the mirrored copy carries on as one smooth curve instead of forming a valley. A switch in Preferences › Drawing.
Zen Mode

The ensō button beside Preferences hides the top bar, the lower rail, the layer strip and the arrange rail, and trims the puck to undo, redo and eraser. A small pill in the corner keeps undo, redo and the way back out. The app remembers it.
Last Drawing widget
A home-screen widget shows the drawing you last opened and opens it with a tap. It refreshes shortly after you switch drawings.
improved: Smoother Across Mirror Lines
The mirror line is now found from each reflection itself, so the bend works with any centre, tile or turn, and it is drawn finely so it reads as one curve rather than facets.
fixed: The eraser group in the tool rail showed an empty button; it shows the eraser again (the circle tool had the same fault).
Lattice shared its icon with the Pattern Gallery; it has its own now.
Opening Preferences, the menu or Export closes any open tool flyout instead of leaving it on screen behind.

title: Lattice, airbrush and a clearer print
summary: Lattice gets its own section of the gallery. The airbrush arrives, any line can be edited as a curve, Live Trace becomes a layer you can re-trace, Print Stencil shows a live preview, panels scroll properly, and you can build your own theme.
new: Airbrush

A soft spray in the brush group. EDGE on the rail switches Soft, Medium and Hard; FLOW sets how much ink one pass lays down, and passes build up. It follows pressure, works in every symmetry copy, and exports with its soft edge.
Live Trace layers
Live Trace previews as you adjust and places the result with ✓ (✕ discards), on its own Live Trace layer that remembers its settings. Select that layer and open Live Trace again to re-trace it.
Edit Curve

Lasso a line and tap Edit Curve: it becomes curve-pen points with smooth handles at its bends, in its own colour, width and symmetry. Drag points and handles, then Done. This works for snapped arcs and S-curves too.
Theme builder
Under Appearance, Customise copies the current theme into your own Custom theme, with a colour picker for each of its eight colours.
Lattices in the gallery
A Drawings / Lattices switch in the gallery bar. Save a lattice and it appears there; tap it to open it again, or start a new one. Send to Canvas from the gallery starts an A4 drawing to receive it.
improved: Print Stencil
A live preview of the stencil, in purple or black, with the page seams marked. Size, ink and layers come first; Lines and Separation fold away with a one-line summary.
Lattice
Geometry Lab is renamed Lattice. It has a Save button, and its layers are named Lattice Lines and Lattice Points.
Preferences
At high roundness the glass and the content share one corner shape, the sidebar title lines up with the section title, and Corners is no longer cut off.
Themes
All fifteen themes show in a grid, with no sideways scrolling.
fixed: Preferences, Print Stencil, Layers and every other scrolling panel now scroll when you drag across their controls.
Print Stencil opens at the largest size that fits one sheet, so an A4 drawing no longer prints across four pages. Larger sizes still tile.
The animated background no longer widens the layout, and the top bar fits a 13-inch iPad in portrait, so the bars and rails keep their margins.

title: A studio of your own
summary: Themes and animated backgrounds make the app feel like yours. The gallery now shows your drawings as artwork, with stacks. The shape builder has the full Illustrator set, and snapping can follow a line you've already drawn.
new: Shape Builder

The full Pathfinder set as icon buttons: Unite, Minus Front, Intersect, Exclude, Divide, Trim, Merge, Crop, Outline and Minus Back, plus Outline Stroke. Drawn lines are outlined automatically, so linework works as well as fills.
Geometry Lab

Recursive geometry built from numbers: points on a circle, each becoming the centre of a smaller copy, level after level, with lines, outlines, star and curve edges, and point circles. It starts simple, previews in your pen colour on paper, and Send to Canvas places it as vector strokes on new layers. On the second rail.
Shape tools in the selection bar
When two or more shapes or lines are selected, the shape modes and pathfinders appear right in the selection bar.
Themes
Fifteen editor-style themes, including Mirage, Midnight, Tokyo Night, Dracula, Nord, Catppuccin and Gruvbox. Each sets the panels, lettering, accent and background colours.
Animated backgrounds
Twelve looping styles from Mirage Core, including Julia, Mandelbrot and Burning Ship fractals, Aurora, Kaleidoscope and Evolving. They run in the gallery and around the page.
Stacks
Drag one drawing onto another to stack them, or use the Stack menu. Open a stack to see what's in it.
Follow snapping
Hold at the end of a stroke drawn beside another line, and it becomes that line's exact parallel at an even gap.
Arc and curve snapping
Holding now snaps a curved stroke to a clean circular arc, or to one smooth curve that handles both C and S shapes.
Lasso on every layer
An option in Preferences takes strokes from every visible layer at once.
improved: Top bar

Each control now opens its own panel, right under it. Rotate, the segment count, Mirror and the centre form one Symmetry group with its own options. Repeat, Tile, Grid (new in the bar) and Fade each have theirs. The pattern button opens just the gallery. Panels are roomier.
Gallery
Drawings appear as sheets of paper with soft shadows, on the animated background, under a glass bar that matches the drawing's top bar.
Preferences
Settings are grouped into six sections in a sidebar: Pencil & Touch, Drawing, Appearance, Background, Haptics and About.
New drawings
A Portrait or Landscape switch, drawings appear in the gallery straight away, and the page opens centred clear of the bars.
Lasso
If nothing on the active layer is caught, the lasso selects on the layer with the most inside it and switches to that layer.
What's New
A fractal header, and a gently pulsing dot on the current build.
Corner Roundness
A Preferences slider for how round panels and bars are.
Labels
Buttons, menus, settings and titles now use Title Case throughout.
Panels
The grab bar is finer and has more room above it, panel buttons have more contrast, and the pin sits centred in its circle.
Curve pen
Available as a shortcut dot around the radial menu.
fixed: A page fitted to the screen no longer touches the top bar or runs under the rails.
A new drawing shows in the gallery even before anything is drawn on it.

title: Preview first, then place
summary: Constructions are previewed before they are placed, and there is a Move tool on the rail. Sliders and panels are lighter, accent colours can be fully customised, and two fill problems are fixed.
new: What's New
This timeline. Open it from the gallery, the menu or Preferences; it also appears once after each update.
Move tool
A Move button on the left rail puts the active layer in the transform box. On the radial menu, the Move dot replaces the Trim dot.
Custom accent colour
A colour picker sits beside the seven preset accents in Preferences.
Accent on guides and selection
Guides, mirror lines, the rope, the lasso and the transform box take the accent colour. A switch in Preferences keeps them separate.
Panel grabber
Every rail panel has a grab bar across its top. Drag it to move the panel anywhere.
improved: Constructions
A construction previews live in your pen colour while you adjust Size, Count and Turn. Nothing is placed until you tap the check mark; the ✕ discards it.
Ink
The fountain pen is now Ink, with an ink-bottle icon. Barrel roll is smoothed point by point, so the nib turns fluidly instead of in steps.
Curve pen
The curve pen has a pen-nib icon and is now the last tool in the brush group.
Glass sliders
Sliders are clear at rest and fill with the accent colour while you drag them, across every panel.
Selection bar
The buttons are clearer. Recolour opens the colour panel and recolours the selection live as you pick.
Rails
The left, right and finishing rails are all the same width.
fixed: Tapping a fill with a new colour recolours it. Before, it removed the fill, so the area looked white.
Fill could cover the whole page after edits elsewhere. Region detection now notices every change, and you're warned before filling anything that covers almost the whole page.

title: After TestFlight
summary: This round added Illustrator-style curves, previewing a design on a client photo, and panels you can move, with readable Liquid Glass throughout.
new: Curve pen
Tap to place corner points, or drag to pull curve handles. Adjust any point afterwards, then close the shape or finish it with Done.
Preview on a photo
Lay the design over a photo of the client, drag its corners to fit it to the limb, and blend it as ink on skin.
Lift the last stroke
One tap moves the line you just drew onto its own layer. Tap again to bring the line before it too.
Movable panels
Rail panels can be dragged anywhere and stay where you put them.
Accent colours
Choose from seven accent colours in Preferences.
Barrel roll
On Apple Pencil Pro, rolling the barrel turns the broad nib as you draw.
Clip and Mask buttons
The layers panel has one-tap Clip and Mask buttons for the selected layer.
Tap the puck for the radial menu
An option in Preferences for a Pencil without squeeze, or for drawing with a finger or a mouse.
improved: Liquid Glass
Panels are tinted so text stays readable over a white page, with a Glass tint slider. The glass now extends to the touch puck and the radial menu.
Constructions
Live preview, a Turn slider, Count up to 24, and an option to place each construction on its own named layer.
Transform box
The turn handle stays reachable near the top of the screen, and the bar no longer runs under the layers panel.
Drawing on a hidden layer
Shows a short notice, and you feel a knock in the Pencil.
Panels
More padding inside panels. Shape builder buttons have icons.
fixed: The Playgrounds copy no longer carries the Xcode development team, which stopped it launching full screen.
It no longer slides under the top bar.
A moved panel no longer leaves its pointer arrow behind.

title: Ready for TestFlight
summary: This round brought colour tracing, layer masks and painting directly on the 3D body, ending in the first TestFlight release.
new: Colour live trace
Turns a photo into stacked colour shapes, from black and white up to 12 colours, and can leave the lightest colour as paper.
Layer masks
Show a layer only inside another layer, or hide it there. Masks work with clipping and in exports.
Paint on the body
Draw directly onto the 3D body in five inks, from 2 to 30 mm.
Wrap onto the skin
A design wraps around an arm or over a shoulder from the spot you tap, instead of being projected flat.
Even steps
An option in Repeat that moves each repeat in by the same distance.
Centre snapping
A layer you move snaps to the page centre and the guide centre.
Diagnostics
A running log you can copy, a note after an unexpected close, and the build number in Preferences.
App icon and TestFlight
The Bismuth crystal is the app icon. Bismuth Studio now installs through TestFlight.
improved: Tracing image
Drag it on the page, lock its position, or send it back to the centre.
Touch puck
Its buttons stay out. A tap no longer opens the radial menu; holding the puck still erases.
3D preview
Dragging, sizing and turning respond faster.
fixed: Builds 87 to 94 didn't compile because of the live-trace code. It was rewritten, and every build is now checked in Xcode before delivery.

title: Tools for the studio
summary: Trimming, text, live trace, clipping and the transform box arrived, along with the staged radial menu and the touch puck.
new: Trim tool
Scribble across a piece of a line to remove it back to the nearest crossings, in every symmetry copy.
Text
Twelve typefaces, filled or outlined, placed as vector shapes on their own layer.
Drawings folder
Keep your drawings, motifs and preferences in a folder such as iCloud Drive, so they carry over between builds.
SVG import
Paths, shapes, fills and colours come in as editable vector shapes.
Live trace
Turns the tracing image into editable fills or outlines, with a live preview.
Clipping layers
A layer shows only where the layer beneath it has ink.
Transform box
Move, resize, stretch and turn a layer directly on the canvas, with an optional proportion lock.
Liner and pressure brushes
The Liner keeps an even width. The tapered fineliner always responds to pressure.
Motif hover ghost
A preview of the motif follows the hovering Pencil and turns with barrel roll.
Built-in bodies
Male and female 3D bodies made from MakeHuman (CC0).
Second rail
Text, Import, Stencil and the 3D body are on a fold-out rail.
Shortcut dots
Fifteen customisable dots around the radial menu.
improved: Radial menu
It opens in stages from the centre with a small bounce, quickly and smoothly.
Touch puck
On by default, with undo, redo, eraser, trim and a context button.
Gradient brush
A colour panel with a preview, Swap and Fade to clear.
Haptics
A soft tick while you drag sliders and dial arcs.
Preferences
Saved in your drawings folder, so they move to a new build with you.
Defaults
The rope stabilizer starts on at 50%, and the radial menu centre shows the five main brushes.
fixed: A trim made as the Pencil lifted was being dropped.
Filling inside a closed shape no longer floods the area around it.
The scribble follows the Pencil exactly, and T-junctions count as cut points.

title: Foundations
summary: The symmetry engine and the core studio: brushes, guides, layers, fills, stencils, motifs and the 3D body preview.
new: Symmetry engine
Mirror, rotate, repeat and tile, with a pattern gallery of 15 presets and an adjustable centre and angle.
Gallery and autosave
Drawings with thumbnails, custom page sizes, rename, duplicate and delete.
Brushes
Pen, fineliner, mechanical pencil, fountain pen, gradient brush, stipple, dots, lines and circles.
Stabilizers
Smoothing and rope, separately or together.
Clean joins
Overshoots where a stroke meets its own symmetry copies are trimmed so the lines meet cleanly.
Fill and shape builder
Vector region fills, dotwork fills, gap tolerance, and Unite and Subtract.
Stencils
Print at the exact finished size, with tiled pages, separation into linework, solids and shading, and thermal-printer images.
Motifs
Capture a layer as a stamp and place it anywhere in the pattern, from a saved library.
Constructions
The Flower of Life, Metatron's Cube, polygons, stars, a golden spiral and more.
Layers
Groups, reordering, swipe actions, and transforming a single layer or a whole group.
3D body preview
Orbit a body and drape the design onto it.
Lasso selection
Select through symmetry copies, then move, recolour, duplicate or delete.
Export
PNG, JPEG, SVG and PDF.
Colour
A custom picker, tattoo palettes, an eyedropper and recent colours.
Import and tracing
A floating reference window and a see-through tracing image.
improved: Radial dial
Three rings: tools, toggles and sliders.
Hold to snap
Recognises lines, circles, ellipses, triangles and rectangles.
Haptics
Distinct pulses for tap, snap, hold, done and undo, with a strength setting.
Preferences and menus
Redrawn in the app's own style.
fixed: Saving moved off the main thread, removing a pause after each stroke.
Thin horizontal gaps were repaired; older drawings are fixed when you open them.
The left-rail panels were rebuilt so they attach to their buttons.
A pinch no longer triggers undo.
